status_at_declaration: Protocol written before training; do not interpret as results
question: Can these tiny models retrieve the first symbol after distractors, at trained lengths and longer unseen lengths?
scope: One easy synthetic associative-free memory test; not intelligence, real text, modern recurrent architectures, or typical production Transformers
task: First token is a uniform target 0..7; intervening distractors are iid 8..15; last token is query16; only final position has target first token; all other labels -1 mask
models: v8 float64 NumPy normalized4head single-block causal Transformer width32 with sinusoidal positions; vanilla tanh recurrent with nearest integer parameter-matched width
length_schedule: Each block of four steps randomly permutes all four lengths; one homogeneous length per batch; seed1000+run_seed. Equal examples at every length; identical per-length token budgets across models.
training_targets: iid uniform 0..7; identical generated batches across models and learning rates for a given run seed
optimizer: Adam beta1=.9 beta2=.999 eps1e-8; global gradient norm clipped1; no weight decay; no early stopping
selection: Separately choose each model's lowest mean query CE in nats across trained validation lengths; first listed LR wins exact ties
evaluation: Exactly128 cases of each target per length, randomly ordered; iid distractors; validation RNG200000+length and test RNG300000+length; fixed across every model/run; evaluation batch16
metrics: Full17-way query crossentropy in nats and full17-way argmax accuracy, mean and individual paired seeds; 12.5% chance for random choice among the8 possible target classes
budget_total: 6 tuning plus6 final runs; 4800 optimizer steps; 2304000 training input tokens and76800 supervised queries
resources: Scratch CPU only, one BLAS thread, no paid resources or production services
